questions.title: The window and document objects
questions.prompt: Using the **document** object, change the page's title (the text in the browser tab) to `Order Form`. Then, using a method of the **window** object, convert the string `"12.5 kg"` to the number 12.5 and store it in `weight` — call the method through `window.` explicitly.

setup.css: body { font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; padding: 1em; }

hints: document.title holds the page title.
parseFloat() is a method of the window object: window.parseFloat(...)
questions.solution:
document.title = "Order Form";
const weight = window.parseFloat("12.5 kg");

questions.title: Textbox and Number objects
questions.prompt: When **Calculate** is clicked, read the `value` of the two text boxes, convert them to numbers, and put the product (rounded to 2 decimals with the Number object's `toFixed()` method) into the `#total` text box. If either value isn't a number, put `Invalid entry` in `#total` instead.

setup.css:
body { font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; padding: 1em; }
label { display: inline-block; margin: .3em 0; }

hints: Text box values are strings: parseFloat(document.querySelector("#price").value)
Use isNaN() to detect bad input.

questions.title: Date objects: format a date
questions.prompt:
Write a function `formatDate(date)` that takes a `Date` object and returns it as `MM/DD/YYYY`, with a leading zero on one-digit months and days.

```
formatDate(new Date(2026, 0, 5))     // "01/05/2026"
formatDate(new Date(2026, 11, 25))   // "12/25/2026"
```

Remember: `getMonth()` counts months from **0**.
hints: getMonth() + 1 gives 1–12. getDate() gives the day of the month.
String(n).padStart(2, "0") adds a leading zero.

questions.title: String object methods
questions.prompt:
Write a function `getDomain(email)` that returns the part of an email address after the `@`, in **lowercase**, using the String methods `indexOf()`, `substring()` (or `slice()`) and `toLowerCase()`. If there is no `@`, return an empty string.

```
getDomain("Grace@Example.COM")   // "example.com"
getDomain("no-at-sign")          // ""
```
hints: indexOf("@") returns -1 when there is no @.
substring(i + 1) returns everything after index i.

questions.title: Three ways to write a function
questions.prompt:
Write the same function three ways. Each takes a `subtotal` and returns the sales tax at 6%, rounded to 2 decimals as a number:

1. a **function declaration** named `taxDeclaration`
2. a **function expression** stored in a constant `taxExpression`
3. an **arrow function** stored in a constant `taxArrow`
hints: Declaration: function name(p) { ... }
Expression: const name = function(p) { ... };
Arrow: const name = p => ...;

questions.title: Global, local and block scope
questions.prompt:
The function in the starter code should return the shipping cost, but calling it throws a **ReferenceError** because of **block scope**. Fix the function (without making `shipping` a global variable) so that:

```
getShipping(30)    // 5.99
getShipping(75)    // 0
```
hints: A variable declared with let inside { } only exists inside those braces.
Declare shipping once, before the if statement, and assign it inside.

questions.title: Attach a click event handler
questions.prompt: When the button is clicked, **toggle** the class `dark` on the `<body>` element, and change the button's text to `Light mode` when dark mode is on and `Dark mode` when it's off. Attach the handler with `addEventListener()`.

setup.html: Some text on the page.
setup.css:
body { font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; padding: 1em; }
body.dark { background: #222; color: #eee; }

hints: document.body.classList.toggle("dark") returns true if the class is now on.

tests.name: One click turns dark mode on
A second click turns it off

questions.title: An anonymous function for a change event
questions.prompt: When the user picks a different option in the `#size` list, show the matching price in `#price` (`$8.00` for small, `$10.00` for medium, `$12.00` for large). Use an **anonymous function** as the `change` event handler.

setup.css: body { font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; padding: 1em; }

hints: The select element's value property is the chosen option's value.
Use if/else or an object like { small: "$8.00", ... } to look up the price.

tests.name: Choosing large shows $12.00
Choosing medium shows $10.00

questions.title: Use the Event object
questions.prompt: As the user types in the `#comment` text area, show how many characters are left out of 50 in `#remaining`, like `42 characters left`. Use the `input` event and the **Event object's** `target` property to read the text. If the count goes below 0, also add the class `over` to `#remaining` (and remove it otherwise).

setup.html: 50 characters left
setup.css:
body { font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; padding: 1em; }
.over { color: #c0392b; font-weight: bold; }

hints: comment.addEventListener("input", evt => { const text = evt.target.value; ... })
classList.toggle("over", left < 0) adds or removes based on the condition.

tests.name: Typing 8 characters shows 42 left
Going over 50 adds class "over"

questions.title: Email List application
questions.prompt:
Like the chapter's Email List application: when the form is submitted, check that

- the first email isn't empty → otherwise `Email is required.`
- the second email matches the first → otherwise `Emails must match.`

Show each message in the `<span>` right after that field (empty string when OK). If there are any errors, **cancel the submit** with the Event object's `preventDefault()` method.
hints: element.nextElementSibling is the span right after an input.
Listen for the form's "submit" event and call evt.preventDefault() when there are errors.

tests.name: Empty email shows "Email is required." and cancels
Mismatched emails show "Emails must match."
Matching emails clear messages and submit
